newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's Sandinistas woo foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's Sandinistas woo foreign investors.

text.p: Leaving behind its Marxist roots, Nicaragua's Sandinista Front Monday promised to embrace the free market if it wins Nicaragua's October 20 presidential election in an effort to ease investor fears.

Polls show former president and current Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega chipping away at the lead of right-wing rival Arnoldo Aleman of the Liberal Alliance, with the two candidates virtually even in the latest poll in Managua.

A field of 22 other candidates trails badly. If no one receives at least 45 percent of the vote on October 20, a second round pitting the top two vote-getters will be held on an as-yet-undetermined date.
"A Sandinista government will obey the rules of the free market and give foreign investors a warm welcome," Sandinista campaign manager Alvaro Fiallos told reporters.

Fiallos said a Sandinista government would even continue the International Monetary Fund's tough structural adjustment programme, though seeking better conditions in some areas, and would welcome foreign assembly plants in its free-trade zone.
To ease foreign investor fears, Ortega recently visited Nicaragua's free-trade zone, meeting with Taiwanese assembly plant owners, promising them a warm welcome under a future Sandinista government.
The move came after Nicaraguan business leaders warned of the negative economic consequences of a Sandinista victory.
The Sandinista Front, once a guerrilla army that came to power in a bloody revolution, has campaigned as a modern centre-left political party this year.

Nicaraguan business mogul Carlos Pellas, scion of the country's richest family, told a local television station foreign investors would avoid Nicaragua for two years following a Sandinista electoral victory while they waited to see the government's attitude toward business.
Pellas said that during the first Sandinista government from 1979-1990, Nicaragua copied the Cuban and Soviet economic models with disastrous consequences for the economy.
The Sandinstas fell from power in the stunning 1990 election upset by President Violeta Chamorro.
